translations.text: He sent them to bring fire. They returned and said that they had found no fire, but only murky water. He ordered them to take some of it and bring it. When the sacrifices and offerings had been brought up, Nehemiah ordered the priests to sprinkle some of it on the wood and the sacrifices.
When they did this, a flame of fire blazed until the light of the fire on the altar had died away.
The king built up the place and made a temple there after investigating the matter.

For our part, we took responsibility for these matters and wrote them in an abridged form. This was not easy for us. Rather, with sweat, toil, weariness, and much sleeplessness, we compared, arranged, and wrote them in an abridged form.
But pursuing brevity of expression and leaving out many details is permitted to someone who tells much in few words in an abridged account.

From here, then, let us begin the accounts mentioned earlier and put together in an abridged form. For it is good for someone to explain and persuade at length before the account, but to tell the account itself briefly.
The evil of his hostility grew so great that many murders were committed by those whom Simon himself incited.
It happened that throughout the city, for about forty days, horsemen were seen racing through the air, dressed in golden robes, holding spears, and equipped with every kind of weapon.
The distress and oppression that all of them suffered were terrible and bitter.

After saying these things, he departed from this world. By his death he left not only the young but also many of the people an example and demonstration of courage and strength, and a glorious memory and remembrance.
After this they brought the third brother, mocking and torturing him. He ordered them to cut out his tongue. Immediately he put out his tongue and gladly stretched out his hands as well.
For you will not escape the judgment of God, who rules over all.
He would enter unexpectedly and destroy cities and villages. He seized the nearby regions, won battles, and killed many.

He said to them, “Look and see the disgrace unjustly inflicted on the holy place by their hands. Give yourselves to the struggle and fight bravely.” He also reminded them of the disgrace and mockery that the city had suffered at their hands, and of their abolition of the ancestral laws.
When they heard these things, they were encouraged, strengthened, and emboldened, and courageously committed themselves to their law and their country. He divided the army into four divisions.

When they returned to their own land, they celebrated their victory in battle. They brought Callisthenes and those with him and burned them in a single house, because they had burned the holy gates and fled. They received punishment fitting their evil and unjust deeds.
Despite all these things, he found no relief from his pains, for God's righteous judgment had overtaken him. When he despaired of his own life, he wrote the Jews the following letter of supplication.
It happened that the temple was purified again on the very same day on which it had been defiled by the nations: the twenty-fifth of the month called December.
Although he had only a few men, he killed more than twenty thousand in their [?] strongholds.
They found Timothy hiding in a pit and killed him there, along with his brother Chaereas and Apollonius.
Many of them, wounded, fled naked. Lysias himself also escaped by fleeing in great disgrace.

Maccabeus agreed to everything Lysias requested, because he wanted the arrangements that would be helpful to take effect. The king granted the Jews everything that Maccabeus had written and sent to Lysias concerning them.

For we have heard that they did not wish to submit to my father's intention of imposing paganism, but wanted to remain faithful to their own laws. For this reason they ask that their laws be left to them.
Stay well. In the year one hundred and forty-eight, on the fifteenth of Nisan.
Therefore hurry to send us someone who can inform us how you are doing.
But the rulers and governors in the regions—Timothy, Apollonius son of Gennaeus, Hieronymus, Ramphon, and Nicanor—and the Cypriots with them would not let them have peace or rest.

He prayed and cried out to God, the righteous judge, and attacked those who had murdered their brothers. They burned their harbor at night, together with the ships in it, and killed those they found aboard them.
Dositheus and Sosipater, commanders and leaders among the followers of Maccabeus, went and killed the men Timothy had left in the fortresses, more than ten thousand men.
While he was singing hymns in the voice of the ancestors, he began killing them. Gorgias and his men were defeated and fled.

With him was Lysias, who had been put in charge of affairs. He had an army drawn from many nations: one hundred and ten thousand infantry, five thousand three hundred cavalry, twenty-two elephants, and three hundred chariots equipped with shields for battle.

He gave those with him the watchword, “God’s salvation,” and took selected, strong young men with him. He went against the camp and attacked the king’s courtyard at night. There he killed about three thousand men, and crushed and brought down the largest of the elephants, together with all its equipment.
To take possession of the whole land, because he had killed Antiochus and Lysias, his chief steward.
Immediately King Demetrius summoned Nicanor, who had been appointed commander over the elephants, a ruler and governor.
They agreed on a day to meet one another. Each of them was surrounded by armed men [?].

When Alcimus saw the affection and harmony between Nicanor and Judas, he went to King Demetrius and told him about Nicanor: “He has become disloyal to your kingdom and to all your affairs, for he has made Judas, who is an enemy of your kingdom, his partner and friend.”
You are the Lord of all, and you need nothing. You chose to select a place for your temple, so that your presence might dwell among us.

His blow failed because of his haste and agitation. When the crowds entered through the courtyard gates, he sprang up onto the wall bravely and forcefully and threw himself into the middle of the crowds.
Onias answered and said about him, “This is Jeremiah the prophet, who loves his brothers and earnestly pleads, makes supplication, and prays for the people and the holy city.”
There was turmoil and panic in his camp. But Judas and his men gave thanks and blessed the Lord in the language of their ancestors.
He cut the wicked man’s tongue out of his head, cut it into small pieces, and ordered that it be given to the birds. He nailed up his hand opposite the temple.
